content.comment_body: I'm having trouble connecting through [product_name] over the internet to my [product_name] device. I use DDNS to connect and can access the device's web server. In [product_name], the connection test shows green, but when attempting to upload or download programs, it only shows 'Connecting to BM Window' and stays stuck there. Firewall on my laptop is off, and the router at the device location has both TCP and UDP connections open. Any suggestions on what might be wrong? Apologies for my English.
Is port 8080 open? You should enter the address as: "MyDynDNSaddress:8080"
On this DDNS address, I have three [product_name] devices: one on port 8085, another on 8086, and a third on 8087.
You didn't mention that in your first post. In that case, you need to use port forwarding to map all three [product_name] devices to port 8080.

I will reach out to the network admin at the facility to update the DDNS addresses as follows: Device 1: www.adres1.ddns.net:8080 Device 2: www.adres2.ddns.net:8080 Device 3: www.adres3.ddns.net:8080 Currently I have: Device 1: www.adres.ddns.net:8085 Device 2: www.adres.ddns.net:8086 Device 3: www.adres.ddns.net:8087 Is my understanding correct that this setup is incorrect?
I'm not sure, as I don't know your network configuration. For example, I use a Fritz! Box router, and port forwarding works differently than in your system.
Thank you for your assistance. I'll try changing the ports to 8080 and let you know if that resolves the issue.

Hello, For port mapping on your router, set external port 8085 and internal port 8080 for device 1 IP, external port 8086 and internal port 8080 for device 2 IP, and external port 8087 and internal port 8080 for device 3 IP. On your local PC, use Domain:8085 to connect to device 1, Domain:8086 for device 2, and Domain:8087 for device 3.

My DDNS is configured as described. When I connect using [product_name], I receive the green line and am prompted for the BM password, which I enter correctly. Then, it just shows the connecting window endlessly. In my hardware settings, remote access, web server, and app server options are enabled.
I can only share my router’s port forwarding settings as an example. Please see the attachment; I'm based in Germany. I have two [product_name] devices.
Hello, perhaps the attached file will assist you further.
Issue resolved. The internal port must be set to 8080 as mentioned; the external port can be any port. Thank you for all the help!

analysis.insight_summary: Users face ongoing connection problems between [product_name] software and hardware using remote internet access. Even though a basic connection test succeeds, full programming operations sometimes hang and do not complete. Complex network setups involving DDNS and port forwarding, along with minimal feedback from the software, lead to confusion and make remote configuration for multiple devices challenging and non-intuitive.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to remotely access each [product_name] device, authenticate, and transfer programs seamlessly using [product_name], with clear, actionable feedback if errors occur. The ideal network setup would easily support several devices on different ports without unnecessary complexity.
